newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African economy robust, BOP improving - Erwin.
newsitem.headline: South African economy robust, BOP improving - Erwin.

text.p: The fact that most South African imports continued to be plant and machinery augured well for robust South African economic growth, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said.
"The interesting thing about imports is that it remains very much machinery and equipment. For me that is a sign that the growth that we are going through is very robust," he told a media briefing.
"Effectively, investors are bringing their goods in despite the increased prices (due to the weaker rand) and that must mean that they have got long term investment plans."
At the same time the lower rand was making exports more competitive.
"There is (now) a quite a large trade surplus in the current account," Erwin noted.

"The underlying situation on the balance of payments is in fact healthy because the exports were growing before the depreciation and they will grow faster with the depreciation." At the same time there were no major long term capital outflows.
"I think the underlying balance of payments is very healthy. What we are getting hammered on is the financial markets."
